candidates.reason: URL utility tests are the closest unit boundary for hostname conversion and can directly pin legacy IDNA fallback behavior alongside existing URL normalization.
Twisted's hostname resolver is the primary runtime consumer of the patched IDNA byte conversion, so resolver tests best expose whether the compatibility hook is effective.
Request construction includes URL normalization before DNS or TLS; this suite verifies that an internationalized hostname is preserved consistently for downstream consumers.
TLS hostname verification also calls Twisted's IDNA helper, and these tests exercise the context-factory boundary where an IDNA-2003-only host must remain valid.
Downloader handler coverage validates the end-to-end request path through endpoint creation and hostname processing without relying only on helper unit tests.
The compatibility patch is intended to run at Scrapy import time; top-level import tests are the narrowest place to catch activation or import-order regressions.
A crawl-level test is the clearest user-facing regression check for reaching a hostname that previously failed during Twisted name conversion.
